You are implementing exactly one bug (#620) on branch bug-620-hands-reaper, already checked out in this worktree off origin/main. The issue text below is the whole framing: its "What is asked" and "Acceptance" sections are what done means. Decision 0071 (the architectural principles) is ACCEPTED, and the house rules' Architecture section states its Rust form. Build to it. Where the issue leaves a choice to the operator, implement the option it recommends (or the first listed), keep it small, and say which you took in your result notes so the pull request can ask for the ruling. If the story is too large for one reviewable commit, deliver the smallest complete slice that meets acceptance items end to end, and name the rest in notes as follow-ups. Do not deliver a half-built everything.

HOST FACTS AND PARALLEL WORK

- Main is origin/main as you find it (bc2dd5f8 or later). #415 introduced the dead-session reaper (crates/brokkr-protocol/src/hands/session.rs: reap_dead_sessions, reap_dead_sessions_in, probe, dead_owner); brokkr-cli's drive_to_end calls it at a run's start and prints what it reaped.
- Operator ruling, 2026-09-26, the threat model: catch realistic ACCIDENTAL misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.
- Tests that spawn processes: since #403 the test binary is a subreaper engine; a test that leaves a process alive runs that launch in a child process of the test binary.
- Other work in parallel: #429 slice 3 (brokkr-core fold.rs), #430 slice 3 (PR #621), #351 slice 3 (PR #623), #367 (docs), and another session's U6c8, which owns brokkr-protocol secret.rs and broker.rs, brokkr-cli broker/*, cli_args.rs and hands/namespace/entry.rs: do NOT touch those, nor observer.rs, agents/mcp.rs or bundle/mcp.rs. hands/session.rs and hands/tests.rs are free.
- THIS IS BUG #620, on branch bug-620-hands-reaper, cut from main and checked out here. The issue below was measured on the operator's host on 2026-10-10: 400 dead brokkr-hands-* trees in /tmp (387 'test', 6 'serve', 7 'exec'), and three exec trees whose overlay/<n>/work/work directory sat at mode 0200 defeated both `rm -rf` and the reaper's remove_dir_all, until `chmod -R u+rwx overlay` made them removable.

DELIVER the issue's three asks, each with exact tests and a compiling removal control recorded in the commit:
1. Reaping a dead tree makes its overlay work directories owner-readable and searchable before removing it. Scope this strictly to `overlay/*/work/work` (and its parents inside overlay/) under a tree this module named (brokkr-hands-<label>-<pid>-<uuid>), whose owner is dead and whose lock is free, never following a symlink and never leaving the tree. Test: a dead exec tree with a 0200 work/work dir, holding a file, is removed.
2. A removal that fails is reported: a Free tree whose removal fails goes to `kept` with its error, so drive_to_end's stderr line names it. Test: the exact line for an unremovable tree; the existing removed and kept lines are unchanged.
3. Tests that create hands sessions do so under a per-test temp dir, or remove what they create on every path, so `cargo test -p brokkr-protocol` leaves no brokkr-hands-test-* in the host's temp dir. Inject the temp dir where the code reads std::env::temp_dir(); do not set TMPDIR in the test process (parallel tests share it). Measure it: before and after a full `cargo test -p brokkr-protocol`, count brokkr-hands-test-* in the temp dir, and record both counts.
- Gates as usual: cargo test -p brokkr-protocol and -p brokkr-cli (crate-scoped), clippy -D warnings, fmt, typos --hidden, quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api. The exact-coverage gate is the controller's. Name any public-API change in notes.

THE ISSUE (#620), verbatim:

## What was found

On the operator's host on 2026-10-10, `/tmp` held **400 `brokkr-hands-*` session trees**, every one with a dead owner and no held `.owner.lock`. That is exactly the set `hands::reap_dead_sessions` exists to remove. By label:

- 387 `test`
- 6 `serve`
- 7 `exec`, 4 of them with an `overlay/` tree

They held about 33 MiB, so size was not the harm. The harm is that they accumulate silently, and that the reaper cannot remove one of the three shapes.

**1. A dead `exec` tree with an overlay can never be reaped.** The overlay's `overlay/<n>/work/work` directory is left at mode `0200` (`d-w-------`), owned by the operator. overlayfs creates its work directory that way. `std::fs::remove_dir_all` cannot list it, so the removal fails with `Permission denied`. Reproduced by hand: `rm -rf` on three such trees failed on `overlay/1/work/work`; `chmod -R u+rwx overlay` first, then removal, succeeded.

**2. A failed removal is reported nowhere.** In `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/hands/session.rs`, `reap_dead_sessions_in` matches `Probe::Free if std::fs::remove_dir_all(&tree).is_ok() => reaped.removed.push(tree)`. A `Free` tree whose removal fails falls to `Probe::Free | Probe::Held => {}`: it is neither in `removed` nor in `kept`, so `drive_to_end` says nothing about it on stderr. Unremovable trees stay forever and invisibly.

**3. The reaper only runs at a run's start.** `brokkr-cli`'s `drive_to_end` calls it before driving. Test runs create sessions in the real temp dir (`Session::create("test")` in `hands/tests.rs`). A test process that dies or is killed leaves its tree for whichever `brokkr run` next starts on that host, and 387 had piled up.

## Asked

- Reaping makes an `exec` tree's overlay work directories owner-writable and readable, scoped to `overlay/*/work/work` under a tree this module named and whose owner is dead, before removing the tree. Test: a dead exec tree with a `0200` work directory is removed.
- A removal that fails is reported: push it to `kept` with its error, so the stderr line names it. Test: the exact line for an unremovable tree.
- Tests that create hands sessions do so under a per-test temp dir, or remove what they create on every path, so a test run leaves nothing in the host's `/tmp`. Measure it: a clean `cargo test -p brokkr-protocol` leaves no `brokkr-hands-test-*`.

Related: #415 (scratch lifecycle), #430 (the scratch floor reads the temp dir's room), #472 (containment).

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

result.notes:
All three asks of #620 are delivered in one commit, 132a61f5 (signed off, GPG-signed, not pushed). (1) A new remove_tree(tree) in hands/session.rs is the one removal of a session's tree. The reaper, Session::drop and remove_on_termination all use it. Before removing, it gives the owner 0700 on overlay/, each overlay/<n>, its work and that work/work, and on nothing else. The walk descends by descriptor (each open is O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY), reads each entry's type with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW and skips . and .., so it never follows a symlink or leaves the tree. (2) A Free tree whose removal fails now goes to `kept` as a new private enum Kept::Unremovable(io::Error), beside Kept::Unprobed. Its line is 'hands: kept <tree>: it cannot be removed: Permission denied (os error 13)'. The removed line and the lock-probe kept line keep their text (existing tests pass unchanged). (3) A new Session::create_under(tmp, label) is pub(super); Session::create calls it with std::env::temp_dir(). The three sessions in hands/tests.rs are now made under their test's tempdir. TMPDIR is not set in any test.

Cause found and widened scope: the leaked brokkr-hands-test-* trees came from Session::drop, not only from killed processes. hands::tests::the_box_hides_the_host_and_holds_the_worktree leaves overlay/0/work/work at mode 0, and Drop's remove_dir_all failed on it. The scratch counter listed nine such trees, all with that shape. A per-test tempdir alone would still have leaked a .tmpXXXX dir holding that tree. So Drop and the termination handler share remove_tree; this was needed for ask 3 to work.

Measurement: a scratch cargo bin (.forge/count, not committed) counts std::env::temp_dir()=/tmp. On unchanged main, a full `cargo test -q -p brokkr-protocol` took brokkr-hands-test-* from 8 to 9. With the change it was 0 before and 0 after a full run (869 passed, 3 ignored, plus the integration binaries).
